security_threats.asset: package identity, publisher trust, provenance, and current revocation state
controls: exact digest and publisher binding
offline signature bundle and trusted roots
role-separated versioned expiring repository metadata
rollback floor and emergency revocation
verify before review or extraction
hostile_mutations: valid signature for another publisher or package
revoked publisher with cached older package
security_threats.residual_risk: Trusted-root and publisher governance remain human and operational authorities that require incident-response ownership.

security_threats.asset: local filesystem, disk capacity, parser memory, and installed generations
controls: verify before extraction
private no-follow staging
portable canonical unique paths
file byte depth and expansion limits
atomic publication and recovery
hostile_mutations: symlink hardlink device fifo or socket
disk full read-only or interrupted publish
verification_owner: disk-full permission link and crash-recovery integration tests
security_threats.residual_risk: Archive and filesystem behavior varies by platform and needs native containment evidence.

security_threats.asset: host process, terminal sessions, credentials, providers, files, network, and capability broker

reject unknown imports and unsupported features
digest scope generation and grant checked host calls
typed output revalidation
no native payloads or direct PTY process network file clipboard or secret path
verification_owner: capability mutation and cross-session isolation tests
security_threats.residual_risk: A runtime escape or host binding bug remains possible; sandboxing is defense in depth and requires prompt updates.

security_threats.asset: input latency, CPU, memory, tables, host allocations, queues, handles, threads, storage, and shutdown
controls: fuel plus emergency deadline
guest and host-transfer resource limits
bounded concurrency queue output logs cache and versions
generation cancellation and stale rejection
crash quarantine and joined teardown
security_threats.residual_risk: Runtime and host allocations not covered by linear-memory limits require same-host measurement and conservative global ceilings.

security_threats.asset: user intent, grants, profiles, sessions, panes, versions, and rollback
controls: default deny and narrow initial capabilities
digest version scope profile and expiry bound grants
fresh review for authority or data-flow changes
revocation before invocation
cross-route and stale-generation denial
verification_owner: update revoke rollback disable and uninstall tests
security_threats.residual_risk: People can approve risky requests; UX must show exact changes and safer alternatives without relying on color.

security_threats.asset: visible trust state, accessible meaning, clipboard/insertion truth, focus, and command review
controls: bounded untrusted plain text
control bidi and markup containment
host-owned icons colors trust badges and risk labels
full accessible values and keyboard focus restoration
copy or insert without Enter and final policy review
verification_owner: accessibility semantics and native screen-reader assessment
security_threats.residual_risk: Unicode confusables cannot be eliminated; source, exact value disclosure, and textual risk reduce ambiguity.

security_threats.asset: manifest, WIT, component features, state schema, support window, and last-known-good data
controls: exact major and bounded minor compatibility
reject unknown fields imports exports and features
side-by-side migration with validation
atomic schema publication and rollback
versioned conformance kit and deprecation policy
hostile_mutations: new SDK with old risk policy
security_threats.residual_risk: The Component Model evolves; supported runtime and SDK versions need a named update owner and explicit release window.

security_threats.asset: selected input, secrets, provider identity, privacy choice, operation risk, and execution authority
controls: separate opt-in and per-request exact data-flow review
selected bounded input only with redaction preview
provider locality model destination purpose and retention disclosure
typed bounded response with independent risk classification
no tools MCP background typing requests or automatic execution

prompt asks for tools or credentials
verification_owner: provider offline timeout cancellation and stale-route tests
security_threats.residual_risk: Selected text can itself contain sensitive data; explicit preview and provider policy cannot replace the user's judgment.

security_threats.asset: package cache, selected input, grants, receipts, profiles, sessions, handles, and user-owned state

selected input memory only
profile and route isolation
